A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CADFit by the same authors. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments, construction-sequence comparisons, runtime measurements and image-to-mesh evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments, revises reported results and adds learned-prior, preprocessing and hyperparameter ablations.

M1.justification: V1 Algorithm 2 unions all candidates before backward pruning; v2 Algorithm 7 starts empty, greedily adds IoU-improving candidates, then prunes. This changes the core search procedure. V2 Appendix M also specifies visual/geometric feature fusion and GELU/dropout, versus v1 Appendix L's visual embedding and ReLU classifier. DINO-based visual encoding itself was already documented in v1.

E1.justification: DeepCAD, Fusion360, ABC complexity subsets and image-to-CAD tasks remain. V2 Table 5 adds direct evaluation on noisy Hunyuan3D meshes without smoothing/decimation, extending tested input conditions. The mechanical-component photo-style demonstration already appeared in v1 Appendix B and is relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: The external benchmark comparators remain GenCAD-3D, CAD-Recode, Cadrille and, for image-to-CAD, CAD-Coder; the Trellis/Hunyuan3D comparison also remains. V2 Table 4 newly evaluates an explicit no-prior comparator using randomly sampled loops. Revised Cadrille scores do not establish a change of external baseline identity.

E3.justification: IoU computation changes from Monte Carlo integration with 100,000 occupancy samples in v1 Appendix C.3 to Boolean intersection/union volumes in v2 Appendix B.3. V2 also introduces a 100-loop random-sampling control, preprocessing comparisons and held-out hyperparameter experiments. Main benchmark sample counts and alignment remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that every retained result was recomputed.

E4.justification: V2 adds learned-prior quality/runtime ablations across ABC splits (Table 4), noisy-versus-preprocessed mesh evaluation (Table 5), and six groups of hyperparameter/source ablations (Appendix H, Table 9). These substantially expand component and robustness evidence. Existing upstream-model comparisons and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: The statistical estimation procedure for IoU changes: v1's Monte Carlo occupancy estimator is replaced by direct Boolean-volume computation. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests; v2's additional means do not add uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises ABC Hard IoU from 0.547 to 0.662 for CADFit and from 0.086 to 0.438 for Cadrille, making Cadrille the strongest baseline there. Median results, Cadrille image-to-CAD scores and Figure 4 outputs also change; CADFit's Table 2 scores remain unchanged. New ablations include a 2.90-fold ABC Hard speedup with the prior. Changed method and IoU computation prevent interpreting benchmark revisions as isolated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix H becomes v2 Appendix G with unchanged assumptions, refinement theorem, pruning lemmas, proofs and derivations after renumbering. The IoU definition remains the same despite the changed computation procedure; no new theoretical guarantee is established.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: executable complex CAD reconstruction through geometric optimization, a rich operation set, compact programs, strong benchmark accuracy/validity and a decoupled image-to-CAD pipeline. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of the prior's role under a candidate budget, noise-induced sketch fragmentation and computational cost, and hyperparameter quality/runtime tradeoffs. It distinguishes initial-pass applicability from residual refinement's watertightness requirements and explicitly includes unsupported intersections among limitations. Existing curved-surface failures are retained, while the explicit non-generative-model caveat is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link, numerical defaults and tested ranges in Table 9, and prior-training details: 16,719 source STLs, STL-level held-out splitting, specified rendering views and geometric loop features. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's approximately 100,000 labeled profiles and generic classifier description. Newly disclosed defaults and splits do not establish changes to previously run experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including SkexGen, ExtrudeNet, SECAD-Net, SolidGen, UCSG-Net, VideoCAD and DINOv2, and replaces the CAD-MLLM citation with Alrashedy et al.'s vision-language CAD work. The related-work organization and positioning around geometry-driven executable-program optimization remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially rewritten around an explicit outer-loop/inner-pass overview and reordered algorithm exposition. Results become Results and Discussion, limitations receive a separate section before the conclusion, and the photo demonstration moves from an appendix into the main text. Appendix organization and method explanations are extensively revised beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: The pipeline diagram is substantially redrawn and moved from Figure 3 to Figure 2. Figure 4 replaces qualitative reconstructions and reorders method rows; three new experimental tables are added. The photo figure is relocated and reduced, one compactness example is removed, and algorithm displays are reorganized, materially changing presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 supplies previously missing evidence for the learned prior and parameter/preprocessing choices, while documenting defaults, training-data provenance and code access. This improves assessability and reproducibility. The benefit is limited by unresolved inconsistencies: Section 4.4 still identifies CAD-Recode as the strongest ABC Hard baseline despite revised tables favoring Cadrille, and the main text specifies ReLU while Appendix M specifies GELU. The evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than a substantial overall quality gain.
